questions.question: How is a folded normal random variable defined?
options: As a count of events in fixed time
As a uniform value on an interval

questions.question: What is the support of a folded normal variable?
What operation creates the folded normal distribution from a normal variable?
When does a folded normal become a half-normal distribution?
options: When the underlying normal mean is zero
When all values are exactly one

questions.question: When is a folded normal useful?
options: When only the magnitude of a normally distributed quantity matters
When the variable is sampled without replacement, no matter which values are selected.

questions.question: Which example can be modeled by a folded normal distribution?
options: The number of heads in ten tosses
Absolute measurement error from a normal error
The number of calls in ten minutes
The time until first success in trials

questions.question: If $Y\sim N(0,1)$ and $X=|Y|$, what distribution does $X$ have?
Which value is impossible for a folded normal random variable?
Quality-control deviations are recorded only by magnitude. Which model may be appropriate?
If $Y=-3$ for one outcome, what value does $X=|Y|$ record?
Why does folding place probability from negative values on the positive side?
options: Because the normal distribution has no negative values
Because $Y$ and $-Y$ both map to the same absolute value

questions.question: How does folded normal differ from lognormal?
options: Folded normal is always negative, while lognormal is always zero
Folded normal uses $|Y|$, while lognormal uses $e^Y$
Folded normal is discrete, while lognormal is Bernoulli
Folded normal counts trials, while lognormal samples without replacement

questions.question: Why is the folded normal support nonnegative even if the original normal has all real support?
options: The normal variable secretly has nonnegative support
The density becomes a probability mass function
Absolute value maps every real input to a nonnegative output

questions.question: If $Y$ is normal with mean $5$, and $X=|Y|$, what distribution is $X$?
A one-dimensional normal displacement is recorded as distance from zero. What distribution describes that distance?
If $Y$ can be negative but only $|Y|$ is observed, what information is lost?
Which construction gives the centred folded normal distribution?
options: Two independent centred normals are combined into a radius.
A centred normal variable is folded onto the non-negative half-line.
A Poisson count is shifted until it becomes non-negative.
A uniform variable is reflected around its median.

questions.question: Both folded normal and Rayleigh describe magnitudes of normal variables. Which dimensional difference separates them?
options: Folded normal is for counts, while Rayleigh is for exact signs
Folded normal is always degenerate, while Rayleigh is always uniform
Folded normal is one-dimensional magnitude, while Rayleigh is two-dimensional magnitude
Folded normal has negative support, while Rayleigh has positive support

questions.question: If $X=|Y|$ and $Y$ is normal, what is $P(X<0)$?
A model says absolute normal error has folded normal support on all real numbers. What is wrong?
options: The variable should be lognormal instead
The absolute value can be negative
